scope: Board of County Commissioners regular and special meetings, Nov 19, 2024 to Oct 22, 2026 (the current seven members)

recusals.minutes: Commissioner Flowers noted that she must recuse herself from voting since she serves on the Board for the Area Agency on Aging of Pasco-Pinellas, which is one of the organizations recommended to receive Social Action funding.

conflictQuestions.minutes: In response to comments and a query by Commissioner Latvala regarding a potential conflict of interest, Attorney White related that the situation is not a prohibited conflict and does not require that he abstain from voting on this item.

rays-bonds.officialTitle: Pinellas County adoption of a Tourist Development Tax Revenue Supplemental Bond Resolution Supplementing Resolution No. 24-42 adopted on July 30, 2024, and approval of the documents to support funding for the design and construction of a new stadium in St. Petersburg to be the new home of the Tampa Bay Rays Major League Baseball franchise.

addFacts.text: The same bond item came up on Nov 19, 2024 and was pushed to Dec 17 by a 6 to 1 vote (Flowers voted no).
Before the Nov 19 vote, Commissioner Latvala asked about a possible conflict of interest. The county attorney said it was not a prohibited conflict and he did not need to abstain.
For the matching budget change, the Clerk received about 121 emails and voicemails in support, 139 in opposition, and 12 emails of concern.

fy27-tentative.officialTitle: Resolutions adopting tentative millage rates and budgets for Fiscal Year 2027 (First Public Budget Hearing).

addFacts.text: County budget staff corrected themselves at the hearing: the tentative budget is a 0.48% increase over the rolled-back rate of 6.1284, not a 0.16% decrease. The rolled-back rate is the rate that would bring in the same tax money as last year. Florida law calls anything above it a tax increase, even when the rate itself goes down, so the county advertised a Notice of Tax Increase.

airport-rental-cars.officialTitle: Award of contract for on-airport rental car concessions services at the St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport.

behavioral-urgent-care.officialTitle: Opioid Abatement Advisory Board's funding recommendation and associated Agreement and Land Use Restriction Agreement with Operation PAR, Inc. for a Behavioral Health Urgent Care Center.

addFacts.text: The center will be run by Operation PAR, Inc., under an agreement approved Sep 24, 2026.

splitVotes.officialTitle:
Case No. CW 26-12 - Pinellas County
Countywide Plan Map amendment from Residential Rural and Scenic/Noncommercial Corridor to Public-Semi-Public and Scenic/Noncommercial Corridor, regarding 2.69 acres more or less, located at 2577 Keystone Road.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Peters, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Changed 2.69 acres on Keystone Road from rural homes to public use
splitVotes.inShort: Sitting as the Countywide Planning Authority, the board changed the countywide land use map for 2.69 acres at 2577 Keystone Road from Residential Rural to Public/Semi-Public, tied to redeveloping an existing community meeting facility there.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Agreement with American Infrastructure Development, Inc. for Passenger Terminal Improvements - Owner’s Representative.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Scott, seconded by Commissioner Peters, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Hired a project manager for the airport terminal upgrade, up to $1.74 million
splitVotes.inShort: The board approved a contract with American Infrastructure Development, Inc. to act as the county's representative on passenger terminal improvements at St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolutions to adopt final millage rates and budgets for Fiscal Year 2027 (Second Public Budget Hearing).
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Peters, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the final Fiscal Year 2027 budgets for the General Fund and Health Department Fund be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Adopted the final 2027 county budget and tax rates
splitVotes.inShort: At the second and final budget hearing, the board adopted the tax rates and budgets for the year starting Oct 1, 2026, for the General Fund, Health Department, EMS and the other county taxing districts.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Petition of Charles and Rita King, to vacate a portion of a 33-foot-wide right-of-way known as Portsmouth Road, lying east of lots 41 through 43, Gulf Breeze Estates, Plat Book 27, Page 57, lying in Section 30-29-16, Pinellas County, Florida.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Peters, seconded by Commissioner Scott, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Gave up the public's right to a 33-foot strip of Portsmouth Road
splitVotes.inShort: Approved a property owners' petition to vacate part of the Portsmouth Road right-of-way next to Gulf Breeze Estates. Vacating means the county gives up its claim to the strip.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Annual certificate of the Non-Ad Valorem Assessment Roll and Resolution increasing the Non-Ad Valorem Assessment for the Lealman Solid Waste Collection and Disposal District.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Scott, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Raised the trash collection charge for Lealman homes to $288 a year
splitVotes.inShort: Lealman residential property owners pay for county trash pickup through a charge on their tax bill. The board raised it to $288 per home per year.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolution adopting an increased Solid Waste tipping fee for Fiscal Years 2027 and 2028.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Peters, seconded by Commissioner Scherer, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Raised the county dump fee for the next two years
splitVotes.inShort: The fee to dump a ton of trash at the county's solid waste facility goes to $63.57 on Oct 1, 2026 and $68.65 on Oct 1, 2027.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Ordinance amending the Pinellas County Code, Chapter 122, related to the County Towing Ordinance.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Peters, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be approved as amended. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Changed the county towing law, adding new fees
splitVotes.inShort: Amended the towing ordinance to allow an emergency fuel surcharge, yearly inflation increases to the base tow rate, and an electric vehicle fee, plus new signage rules.

splitVotes.officialTitle:
County Administrator Reports:
·	TEFRA Hearing scheduled for July 21 BCC meeting
·	CDBG-DR Update
·	Towing Update
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Peters, that the Board move forward with a base tow rate of $175.00, a mileage rate of $60.00, and a storage rate of $35.00. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Set new maximum towing rates: $175 a tow
splitVotes.inShort: Resolution No. 26-46 set the county's towing rates at a $175 base tow, $60 mileage rate and $35 storage rate.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Term Sheet for the redevelopment and improvements to the BayCare Ballpark Stadium Facility inclusive of BayCare Ballpark, Phillies Complex, and Carpenter Complex.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Vice-Chair Latvala, seconded by Commissioner Nowicki, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Agreed to put $85 million toward upgrading the Phillies' spring training ballpark
splitVotes.inShort: Approved a term sheet to redevelop BayCare Ballpark, the Phillies Complex and the Carpenter Complex in Clearwater. The county's share is expected to come from the tourist development tax.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Revisions to the Capital Projects Funding Program Guidelines from the Tourist Development Council for Fiscal Year 2026.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Peters, seconded by Commissioner Scott, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Changed the rules for tourist tax grants to big local projects
splitVotes.inShort: Revised the guidelines for how tourist development tax money is awarded to capital projects. A point system for geographic spread was removed, and language about waivers for projects asking over $10 million was dropped.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolution adopting an increased Solid Waste tipping fee for Fiscal Year 2026.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Peters, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Raised the county dump fee to $58.86 a ton
splitVotes.inShort: Raised the solid waste tipping fee to $58.86 per ton, effective Oct 1, 2025.

splitVotes.officialTitle:
Case No. FLU-25-09 (Green Energy for North America, LLC) 
A request for a Future Land Use Map amendment from Residential Urban to Residential Medium on approximately 18.43 acres located at 13400 Pine Street in unincorporated Largo.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Scott, seconded by Commissioner Nowicki, that the item be denied without prejudice. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Turned down denser housing on a former landfill site in Largo
splitVotes.inShort: Denied a request to change 18.43 acres at 13400 Pine Street from Residential Urban to Residential Medium, which would allow more homes per acre. The site was once a construction debris landfill. The denial leaves the owner free to apply again.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Revision to the Fiscal Year 2026 Elite Event Funding Recommendations from the Tourist Development Council.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Latvala, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Raised tourist tax funding for 49 local events to $2.76 million
splitVotes.inShort: Revised the 2026 funding list for events paid for with tourist development tax money, up to $2,755,000 for 49 events.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Memorandum of Understanding between Pinellas County and the University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences for salary and fringe.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Vice-Chair Eggers, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Renewed cost-sharing for UF/IFAS county extension staff
splitVotes.inShort: Renewed the county's agreement with the University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences to share the salary and benefit costs of extension staff.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Agreement with Horne LLP for requirements of services for the management, administration and implementation of Community Development Block Grant -Disaster Recovery Program.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Scherer, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Hired a firm to run the $813 million hurricane recovery grant program
splitVotes.inShort: Contracted with Horne LLP to manage the county's federal Community Development Block Grant disaster recovery program.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolutions to adopt final millage rates and budgets for Fiscal Year 2026 (second public hearing).
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Peters, that the final Fiscal Year 2026 budgets for the General Fund and Health Department Fund be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Adopted the final 2026 county budget
splitVotes.inShort: Final approval of the General Fund and Health Department budgets for the year that started Oct 1, 2025.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolutions adopting tentative millage rates and budgets for Fiscal Year 2026 (first public hearing).
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Latvala, seconded by Commissioner Peters, that the tentative budget be amended, as discussed at the August 28 work session and as recommended by the County Administrator in a memorandum distributed to the members on September 3. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Set tentative 2026 tax rates and budgets
splitVotes.inShort: After the deeper cut failed, the board approved tentative tax rates and budgets for the General Fund, Health Department, EMS, Planning Council and other districts.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolutions adopting tentative millage rates and budgets for Fiscal Year 2026 (first public hearing).
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Scherer, seconded by Commissioner Nowicki, for a 50% rollback and a millage rate of 4.5049. The motion failed by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Rejected a deeper property tax cut
splitVotes.inShort: Commissioner Scherer moved to cut the general county tax rate to 4.5049 mills, halfway back to the rolled-back rate. He said the tentative budget was only about $5 million away from that. The motion failed.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Annual certificate of the Lealman Solid Waste Collection and Disposal District Non-Ad Valorem Assessment Roll.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Peters, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Set the 2025 Lealman trash collection charge at $288 per home
splitVotes.inShort: Certified the yearly trash collection charge on Lealman residential tax bills at $288 per unit through Dec 31, 2025.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Agreement with Keep Pinellas Beautiful, Inc. for Adopt-A-Program Management Services.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Vice-Chair Eggers, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Gave Keep Pinellas Beautiful a $1.94 million, 5-year contract
splitVotes.inShort: Approved a 60-month contract with Keep Pinellas Beautiful, Inc. to manage the county's Adopt-A-Program services.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Fiscal Year 2026 Elite Event funding recommendations from the Tourist Development Council.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Commissioner Latvala, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Spent up to $2.69 million in tourist tax money on local events
splitVotes.inShort: Funded 2026 events such as the Firestone Grand Prix, Valspar Championship, St. Pete Pride and the Clearwater Jazz Festival with tourist development tax money.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolution making a finding that conditions of blight exist within the Central Tarpon Springs study area, establishing the Community Redevelopment Area boundary, authorizing the preparation of the Central Tarpon Springs Redevelopment Plan, and delegating redevelopment authority to the City of Tarpon Springs.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Flowers, seconded by Vice-Chair Eggers, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Declared central Tarpon Springs blighted to start a redevelopment district
splitVotes.inShort: Found that blight exists in central Tarpon Springs, set the boundary of a Community Redevelopment Area, and handed redevelopment authority to the city. In a CRA, future growth in property taxes there is set aside for improvements in that area.

splitVotes.officialTitle:
County Commission New Business:
Pertinent and timely Committee/Board updates, policy considerations, administrative/procedural considerations, and other new business:

- Duke Energy Clean Energy Resolution - Commissioner Nowicki
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Nowicki, seconded by Commissioner Scherer, that the item be approved as amended. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Pulled the county out of Duke Energy's Clean Energy Connection program
splitVotes.inShort: Commissioner Nowicki's resolution directs the county administrator to withdraw the county from Duke Energy's Clean Energy Connection program.

splitVotes.officialTitle:
Case No. ZON-24-05 (Dushyant Gulati)
A request for a zoning change from R-R, Rural Residential and R-3-CO, Single-Family Residential with Conditional Overlay to R-3-CO, Single Family Residential with Conditional Overlay on approximately 3.2 acres located at 2281 Kersey Road and 1736 Winchester Road in unincorporated Largo. (Quasi-Judicial) (Companion to No. 24)
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Scherer, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be approved as amended. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Rezoned 3.2 acres on Kersey Road for more single-family homes
splitVotes.inShort: Approved a rezoning at 2281 Kersey Road and 1736 Winchester Road in unincorporated Largo, with a 70-foot minimum lot width added as a condition.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Recommendation from the Tourist Development Council to fund five Fiscal Year 2024 Capital Projects Funding Program applications.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Vice-Chair Eggers, seconded by Commissioner Nowicki, that the item be approved, as amended. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Gave up to $26.4 million in tourist tax money to five building projects
splitVotes.inShort: Funded five capital projects recommended by the Tourist Development Council, after amendments, for up to $26.4 million.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Resolution electing to not exempt property under Section 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes, commonly known as the Live Local Act Property Tax Exemption.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Vice-Chair Scott, seconded by Commissioner Eggers, that the item be approved. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Opted out of a state tax break for some workforce housing
splitVotes.inShort: Florida's Live Local Act lets counties choose whether to give a 75% property tax exemption to rental units for households earning 80% to 120% of area median income. Pinellas chose not to give it.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Request for a public hearing to appeal the issuance of County Dredge and Fill Permit No. WND-24-00077 for 106 Harbor Drive, Palm Harbor.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Vice-Chair Scott, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be denied. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Refused to hold a hearing on a dredge permit appeal in Palm Harbor
splitVotes.inShort: Declined a request for a public hearing to appeal a county dredge and fill permit for 106 Harbor Drive. The county attorney said hearing the appeal was up to the board.

splitVotes.officialTitle: Selection of the 2025 Chair and Vice-Chair.
splitVotes.motion: A motion was made by Commissioner Latvala, seconded by Commissioner Nowicki, that Commissioner Eggers serve as the BCC Vice-Chair for 2025. The motion carried by the following vote:
splitVotes.headline: Picked the 2025 chair and vice chair
splitVotes.inShort: The board chose its leaders for 2025. Commissioner Scott was set to become chair in January.
